 This pink store is Olive Young’s. Why isn't it green? 
 Published : Nov. 20, 2026 - 17:13:57
 No Kyung-min 
 Add The Korea Herald on Google
 Link copied!
 Beauty retailer distills years of know-how into makeup-only store to color K-beauty’s unsung category
 The first floor of Olive Young’s Color Ground Hongdae in Mapo-gu, Seoul (No Kyung-min/The Korea Herald) CJ Olive Young’s first makeup-focused store opened Friday in Seoul’s Mapo-gu in a shade of hot pink — a bold break from the retailer’s signature green.
 The outpost delivers a pointed signal to an industry steeped in skincare that K-beauty’s next surge belongs to makeup, a category long relegated to the sidelines but steadily gaining ground.
 Skincare accounts for 8 or 9 of every 10 K-beauty products exported, while color cosmetics make up about 1. Yet Olive Young’s makeup sales have grown an average of 36 percent a year over the past five years.
 "Skincare alone cannot shake up the mainstream of the global market," an Olive Young official said during a media tour Friday. "The clear, translucent complexion that made K-beauty famous only comes together with makeup."
 Olive Young’s makeup store, Color Ground Hongdae, in Mapo-gu, Seoul (No Kyung-min/The Korea Herald) A store built in layers
 The four-story building’s curved, voluminous facade evokes makeup products, while its hot pink channels the energy of color cosmetics and young shoppers’ beauty culture.
 Inside, each floor carries its own hue, moving from pink on the first floor to lavender on the second and Olive Young’s familiar green on the third.
 The store carries about 200 brands and 1,100 product lines, with twice as many makeup brands as a regular Olive Young. Products are grouped by type, texture and function instead of by brand.
 "We’ve distilled years of know-how into a single category and broken with the usual retail playbook," the official said.
 The ground floor opens with some 300 miniature products, from tiny lipsticks to fragrance key rings, displayed on a Ferris wheel and a carousel. Base makeup is sorted from dewy glow to soft matte, with foundations stocked in each brand’s widest shade range, men’s formulas included.
 Amorepacific’s Hera blends custom foundation to match each shopper’s measured skin tone, and full-time beauty consultants offer walk-in touch-ups.
 "You can simply book on-site, and it takes about 15 minutes," the official said.
 The first floor of Olive Young’s Color Ground Hongdae in Mapo-gu, Seoul (No Kyung-min/The Korea Herald) Upstairs, the lavender floor gathers eye, lip and blush products under adjustable lighting that reveals subtle shades and shimmer. A device diagnoses each customer’s personal color, and shoulder-strap baskets with built-in mirrors free both hands for testing.
 For foreign shoppers, Olive Young is leading with what it calls functional makeup, including primers, setting sprays and lip conditioners, which suit users of any skin tone, ethnicity or gender.
 Short how-to videos throughout the store show how products work, while some foreign-language-speaking staff and an artificial intelligence translation service assist visitors from abroad.
 On the third floor, newcomers take center stage. One in 4 makeup brands in the store makes its Olive Young debut there, and a dedicated shelf spotlights 10 rookies never before sold by the retailer.
 "Our in-store rankings let shoppers see Olive Young’s own data and the latest makeup trends at a glance," the official said.
 The top floor offers a bargain zone, a prize machine for shoppers who spend above a set amount and a lounge.
 The first floor of Olive Young’s Color Ground Hongdae in Mapo-gu, Seoul (No Kyung-min/The Korea Herald) For Olive Young, the store is the first step in taking Korean makeup global, a journey in which promising domestic brands will lead the way.
 That matters all the more because many of them have no offline outlets of their own. What those brands miss in distribution, they make up for in product quality and originality, and Olive Young sees "boundless global growth potential" for Korean makeup.
 The retailer hopes the brands that debut in Hongdae will gain a following among foreign tourists and eventually land in its US stores. It kept the goal loosely defined, however, citing differences in each brand’s circumstances.
 As for additional makeup-focused stores, none are in the works yet. Instead, it continues to fine-tune its retail formats to keep pace with demand and stay ahead of the industry, Olive Young stated.
 The second floor of Olive Young’s Color Ground Hongdae in Mapo-gu, Seoul (No Kyung-min/The Korea Herald)
